title: An earlier video said the heat pump tax credit ran through 2033. The IRS says it ended in 2025.

scenes.purpose: Open on the claim in the channel's own words, as a quotation and nothing else, so the viewer hears what was said before anything is said about it.

visual.description: Portrait frame on the institution's ground, no intro. The large opening quotation mark sets in the accent at the top of the content band, then three ruled lines of the quotation set in the italic display serif, each arriving as its words are spoken: 'technically these heat' / 'pump tax credits ...' / 'available through 2033'. The ellipsis on the second line is the elision, so the last line is read as the tail of the same sentence and not as a second quotation. Earlier lines stay lit; nothing dims, nothing moves after the third line lands. The speaker is named only in the citation block beneath, never set as part of the quotation.

scenes.direction: Cold open: the quotation mark is already setting as the first word lands. The narration spends its first four seconds dating the quotation ('In an earlier video ...'), so hold the band empty but for the quotation mark until the quoted words begin; then build line 1 on 'technically', line 2 on 'pump tax credits' and line 3 on 'available'. If a line fails to align to its words, pin it with a line:N cue in render.json rather than letting the tail appear before it is spoken. Hold all three lines through the pause.
scenes.narration: In an earlier video, The Thought Provocateur told viewers, "technically these heat pump tax credits based on the bill that was signed are available through 2033".

scenes.purpose: Give the credit its real size before it is taken away, so the Short never implies the viewer was promised nothing: a rate with its denominator and the ceiling that bounded it.

visual.description: The quotation clears. Two ledger tiles stack in the content band under the muted line 'The credit, from 2023', each with the accent rule down its left edge. The upper tile counts up to 30% on the word 'thirty' with its label 'Of the cost' beneath; the lower counts up to $2,000 on 'two thousand' with 'Cap each year' beneath. The rate lands first and the cap second, in the order the sentence says them, so the ceiling is read as a limit on the rate rather than as a separate amount. Both tiles hold, unchanged, through 'from 2023'.

chart.title: The credit, from 2023
chart.note: The IRS page: the credit equals 30% of qualified expenses, with $2,000 the most claimable in any year for a qualified heat pump. A credit against federal tax owed, not a payment, and not the price of the equipment.

scenes.direction: Hard cut from the quotation to the tiles. The rate tile counts up on 'thirty', the cap tile on 'two thousand'; 'Of the cost' and 'Cap each year' are labels the narration does not speak, so let each fade in a beat after its figure has settled. Hold both tiles to the end of the sentence.
scenes.narration: The credit was real while it lasted: 30 percent of the cost of a qualifying heat pump, capped at $2,000 a year from 2023.

scenes.purpose: Put the IRS's own sentence on screen, so the end of the credit is read from the record rather than asserted, with the deadline and the words that bound it visible together.

visual.description: The tiles clear to a paper card filling the content band: the document and line numbers in small mono across the top, the passage set in the serif beneath. The window opens on the termination table's 25C row, so 'Energy efficient home improvement credit' and 'The credit will not be allowed' are already legible when the card lands; the words 'for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025' underline in the accent as they are spoken. The underline stops there: the second half of the sentence, about a qualifying heat pump already in service, is carried by the captions the video draws, with nothing new on the card, so the exception is heard against the same passage that states the limit.

excerpt.highlight: for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025

scenes.direction: Cut to the card on 'But it was cut short'. The highlight draws across the passage as its words are spoken and then holds. Hold the card unchanged through 'can still claim it' - the qualification is the beat, not a new graphic - and through the pause that follows, which is the longest in the Short.
scenes.narration: But it was cut short: the IRS says it is not allowed for any property placed in service after December 31, 2025; a qualifying heat pump in service before that deadline can still claim it.

scenes.purpose: Fix the scope of what ended: two federal code sections the IRS lists, and state and utility rebates as separate programmes this Short says nothing about either way.

visual.description: The card clears. Three ruled lines build down the content band, one as its words are spoken: 'Ended: 25C and 25D', then 'Both federal credits', then 'State rebates: separate'. Each earlier line stays lit and dims slightly as the next arrives, so the third line is read as a boundary on the first two rather than as a fourth finding. No tick, no cross and no mark of approval beside any line: nothing here says a rebate is open.

scenes.direction: Hard cut from the paper card. Line 1 enters on '25C beside 25D'; line 2 carries 'federal', which the narration speaks at the head of the sentence, so pin it with a line:2 cue early rather than letting it wait; line 3 enters on 'state and utility rebates'. 'Both' and 'credits' on line 2 are words the narration does not speak in this sentence - let the line settle quietly, no emphasis, no movement. Hold all three lines to the end of the sentence.
scenes.narration: And what ended is federal: the IRS lists it by code section, 25C beside 25D; state and utility rebates are separate programmes.

scenes.purpose: Hand the viewer to the full inquiry; the video draws this as the end card.

visual.description: End card drawn by the video: the institution's seal, the full inquiry's question and the call to action. No lines of its own.

scenes.direction: Dissolve from the lines to the end card. Hold to the last word and a beat after.
scenes.narration: What a heat pump really costs is the question the full inquiry takes on.
